```{r}
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| include: FALSE

library(tidyverse)
library(gutenbergr)
library(spelling)

user_spellpkg <- find.package("spelling")
spell_check_package(pkg = user_spellpkg)
spell_check_setup(pkg = user_spellpkg)
guten_path <- find.package("gutenbergr")

text_vec <- c("the", "quck", "brown", "jumped", "over", "the", "laziy", "dog")

saved_data <- "C:\\Users\\nkuns\\OneDrive\\Documents\\SDS_F26_Namgyal\\SDS264_F26\\r_tip_spell_files\\spellcheck_this.txt"

spellcheck_this <- read.delim("spellcheck_this.txt", header = FALSE)

us_words <- c("color", "savor", "favorite", "honor", "airplane", "jewelry")

ex_string <- "My name is Namgyal Kunsang, and I'm a student at Saint Olaf College! It is raining a lot this week. I wonder when it's going to snow?"

```


## Spelling 

The `spelling` package is a useful tool if you want to double-check a body of text 
for any spelling errors that could impede how it runs. 

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
`Useful Functions:`
:::

:::{style = "font-size: 70%;"}
::: incremental

-   spell_check_text(), 
    -   spell_check_files()
-   spell_check_package()
    -   spell_check_setup()
-   get_wordlist()
    -   update_wordlist()
    
:::
:::

::: footer
More information: [Spelling Documentation](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/spelling/index.html
)
:::

## Arguments {auto-animate="true" auto-animate-easing="ease-in-out"}

::: incremental
-   `pkg`: Path to package's 'root directory'
-   `vignettes`: default FALSE, spellchecks vignettes of a given package
-   `lang` - either "en-US" or "en-GB"
-   `path` - the path
-   `text` - chr vector
    
:::



## Root directory?? {auto-animate="true" auto-animate-easing="ease-in-out"}

- Much like any file in R, each package that you save to your libraries within a working project directory has a stored path.

The root directory is the top level folder where R saves your files when you later need a path to a certain object. 

```{.r code-line-numbers="1|2"}
find.package("gutenbergr")
guten_path <- find.package("gutenbergr")
```

::: footer
More information: [Working Directory](https://intro2r.com/work-d.html)
:::

## Vignettes {auto-animate="true"}

Depending on the package, vignettes might exist as a long documentation showing an extensive guide to a certain package. Kind of like the R Tip of the Day presentations... 

- You can check if a given package has one using the `browseVignettes()` function. 

It looks something like this! 

[browseVignettes("gutenbergr")](http://127.0.0.1:30065/session/Rvig.10c284f554e3c.html) 


::: footer
More information: [Vignettes ](https://r-pkgs.org/vignettes.html)
:::

## Package and Vignette Checking {auto-animate="true"}

:::{style = "font-size: 120%;"}
```r
spell_check_package(pkg = guten_path, vignettes = TRUE)

spell_check_setup(pkg = guten_path, vignettes = TRUE, lang = "en-US")
```

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
```{r}
spell_check_package(pkg = guten_path, vignettes = TRUE)
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
```{r}
spell_check_setup(pkg = guten_path, vignettes = TRUE, lang = "en-US")
```
:::

:::

## That's great, but how can *I* use it? {.smaller .scrollable transition="slide"}

```r
text_vec <- c("the", "quck", "brown", "jumped", "over", "the", "laziy", "dog")

spell_check_text(text_vec, ignore = character(), lang =  "en_US")
```
::: {.fragment .fade-up}
```{r}
spell_check_text(text_vec, ignore = character(), lang =  "en_US")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```r
spell_check_text("I waint to truy aun appel", ignore = character(), lang = "en_US")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
```{r}
spell_check_text("I waint to truy aun appel", ignore = character(), lang = "en_US")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```r
spell_check_text("The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog", ignore = character(), lang = "en_US")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
```{r}
spell_check_text("The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog", ignore = character(), lang = "en_US")
```
:::

## en-US? en-GB? {.smaller .scrollable transition="slide"}

You may or may not have noticed that we've been specifying the language to be `en-US` so far. What happens if we change that?

::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```{r}
us_words
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```r
spell_check_text(us_words, ignore = character(), lang =  "en-GB")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```{r}
spell_check_text(us_words, ignore = character(), lang =  "en-GB")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
Compared to:
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```r
spell_check_text(us_words, ignore = character(), lang =  "en-US")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```{r}
spell_check_text(us_words, ignore = character(), lang =  "en-US")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
Interestingly (or not), R defaults `lang` to en-US. Removing it will give us the same result.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```r
spell_check_text(us_words, ignore = character())
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```{r}
spell_check_text(us_words, ignore = character())
```
:::



## What if I want to add a new word? {.scrollable transition="zoom"}

```r
ex_string
```
::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```{r}
ex_string
```
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-up}
```{r}
spell_check_text(ex_string, ignore = character(), lang = "en_US")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-down}
```r
spell_check_text(ex_string, ignore = c("Namgyal", "Kunsang"), lang = "en_US")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
```{r}
spell_check_text(ex_string, ignore = c("Namgyal", "Kunsang"), lang = "en_US")
```
:::

## Limitations (no package is perfect) {.scrollable transition="fade"}

::: incremental

-   Root directories are a pain to work with (and find)
-   Focused primarily towards people who are writing R packages
-   Only supports English
-   Picky with dataframes
    
:::
